title: Canonical derived Tor-test comparison for exact adjoints
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be symmetric monoidal abelian categories with chosen ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and derived tensor products $\otimes^L$, computed by K-flat resolutions (a complex is K-flat if its direct-sum total tensor with every acyclic complex is acyclic). Let $E:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $R:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ be additive exact functors with a specified adjunction $E\dashv R$. Put $J=D(E)$ and $D(R)$ for their termwise functors. Suppose $P=LR$ is a chosen total left derived functor with its exact-functor comparison $\alpha:P\xrightarrow{\sim}D(R)$, compatible with the derived counit. Use the derived adjunction $J\dashv P$ transported along $\alpha$ from the localized adjunction of [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction]; write its unit as $\eta$ and its counit as $\varepsilon$. Give $P$ its specified strong monoidal structure with tensor map $\mu_{A,B}:PA\otimes^LPB\to P(A\otimes^LB)$.

Assume that for every $K\in D(\mathcal A)$ and $L\in D(\mathcal B)$ the canonical comparison
$$q_{K,L}=\varepsilon_{JK\otimes^LL}\circ J(\mu_{JK,L})\circ J(\eta_K\otimes1):J(K\otimes^LPL)\longrightarrow JK\otimes^LL$$
is invertible. Let $N[0]$ denote the complex with $N$ in degree zero and zero elsewhere. Write $\sigma_N:D(R)(N[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}(RN)[0]$ for the termwise single-complex comparison. Then
$$\tau_{K,N}=J(1_K\otimes(\sigma_N\alpha_{N[0]}))\circ q_{K,N[0]}^{-1}:JK\otimes^LN[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}J(K\otimes^L(RN)[0])$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal B)$, natural in $K,N$. For all integers $a,b$, if $H^q(K\otimes^LA[0])=0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$ and $q\notin[a,b]$, then $H^q(JK\otimes^LN[0])=0$ for every $N\in\mathcal B$ and the same $q$. No boundedness, constructibility, regularity of a coefficient ring, or common projective-resolution hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For $f:K\to K\prime$ and $g:L\to L\prime$, naturality of the unit of the specified transported adjunction [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction] and of the monoidal structure gives $(PJf\otimes^LPg)(\eta_K\otimes1)=(\eta_{K\prime}\otimes1)(f\otimes^LPg)$ and $P(Jf\otimes^Lg)\mu_{JK,L}=\mu_{JK\prime,L\prime}(PJf\otimes^LPg)$. Naturality of the counit gives $(Jf\otimes^Lg)\varepsilon_{JK\otimes^LL}=\varepsilon_{JK\prime\otimes^LL\prime}JP(Jf\otimes^Lg)$. Apply $J$ to the first two equations and compose with the third. Thus $(Jf\otimes^Lg)q_{K,L}=q_{K\prime,L\prime}J(f\otimes^LPg)$: the specified $q$ is natural in both variables.

source.place: Finite Tor amplitude paragraph: returned step 4, comparison Lj^*(N[0]) with (j^*N)[0] and transfer of the fixed interval through the canonical projection map.

proof.text: Put $\beta_N=\sigma_N\alpha_{N[0]}:P(N[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}(RN)[0]$. The termwise single-complex comparison is the one of [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], applied to the exact functor $R$. Before localization it is the identity on $RN$ in degree zero and the canonical zero-object identification elsewhere. Hence for $n:N\to N\prime$, $\sigma_{N\prime}D(R)(n[0])=(Rn)[0]\sigma_N$. Combining with naturality of the supplied $\alpha$ gives $\beta_{N\prime}P(n[0])=(Rn)[0]\beta_N$. Each $\beta_N$ is invertible, so $d_{K,N}=J(1_K\otimes^L\beta_N)$ is an isomorphism, natural in $K,N$, by bifunctoriality.

source.place: Finite Tor amplitude paragraph: returned step 4, comparison Lj^*(N[0]) with (j^*N)[0] and transfer of the fixed interval through the canonical projection map.

proof.text: Every $q_{K,N[0]}$ is invertible by hypothesis. Define $\tau_{K,N}=d_{K,N}q_{K,N[0]}^{-1}$, exactly the displayed map in the statement. Its inverse is $q_{K,N[0]}J(1_K\otimes^L\beta_N^{-1})$; the two composites are identities by functoriality and cancellation. Multiplying the naturality equation of Step 1 on both sides by the appropriate inverses gives $q_{K\prime,N\prime[0]}^{-1}(Jf\otimes^Ln[0])=J(f\otimes^LP(n[0]))q_{K,N[0]}^{-1}$. Compose with $d_{K\prime,N\prime}$ and use Step 2 to obtain $\tau_{K\prime,N\prime}(Jf\otimes^Ln[0])=J(f\otimes^L(Rn)[0])\tau_{K,N}$. This proves naturality of the isomorphism for arbitrary derived $f$ and arbitrary $n$.

source.place: Finite Tor amplitude paragraph: returned step 4, comparison Lj^*(N[0]) with (j^*N)[0] and transfer of the fixed interval through the canonical projection map.

proof.text: Fix $N\in\mathcal B$ and $q\notin[a,b]$, and put $T=K\otimes^L(RN)[0]$. Since $RN\in\mathcal A$, the hypothesis gives $H^q(T)=0$. Apply $H^q$ to $\tau_{K,N}$ and then use [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below] with the exact functor $E$ and the unbounded object $T$: $H^q(JK\otimes^LN[0])\cong H^q(JT)\cong E(H^q(T))=0$. Additivity gives $E(0)=0$, since $1_{E0}=E(1_0)=E(0)=0$. The same integers $a,b$ work for every $N$; this also applies when $a>b$. All objects used belong to the ordinary unbounded categories; no resolutions or boundedness assumptions were introduced.

Step 3: τ=d∘q^{-1} has inverse q∘J(1⊗β^{-1}), and the conjugated naturality equation has the right orientation. Step 4: T=K⊗(RN)[0] with RN in A, so H^q(T)=0 outside [a,b]; then H^q(JK⊗N[0]) ≅ E(H^q T) = 0 by lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below, which holds for unbounded K.
